name: Prepare the rebasing rate application (five-year Custom IR)
summary: Every five years the utility asks the Ontario Energy Board to reset its distribution rates on a five-year Custom Incentive Rate-setting plan. The regulatory affairs team runs a project of about two and a half years: customer engagement and benchmarking feed a business plan and Distribution System Plan, analysts turn them into exhibits and OEB workforms, and after filing the utility answers written interrogatories, sits a technical conference, negotiates a settlement with intervenors and argues any unsettled issue before the OEB issues a decision and rate order. It is slow because each stage waits for the one before it, for the OEB's procedural calendar and for eight or so intervenors, and error-prone because the same numbers must agree across thousands of pages and dozens of linked spreadsheets.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario electricity distributor with about 350,000 customers, filing a five-year Custom IR application with a revenue requirement of about $200M.
baseline.notes: Modelled on Hydro Ottawa's 2021-2025 application (EB-2019-0261), engagement launched January 2019 and final rate order around the start of 2021. COVID-19 moved the 2020 proceeding to virtual conferences and electronic-only filing.

trigger: The current rate plan is entering its last two years, and the capital plan and board direction call for a rebasing application for the next five-year term.
end_state: The OEB has issued a final rate order and approved tariff for the new term and the regulatory team has handed them to rate implementation.

volume.seasonality: One application every five years, timed so that the final rate order lands before January 1 of the first rate year; filing usually happens in the first quarter of the year before.

evidence.note: Five-year Custom IR term, January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2025 (s1).
Role and cost from the organisation file. Leads the application; FTE is averaged over the five-year cycle (about 0.7 FTE in the two busy years).
Regulatory staff prepare the Chapter 2 appendices and workforms (s4). FTE is averaged over five years; in the filing year most of the seven analysts work on the application.

roles.title: Vice-President (operations, engineering, customer service, finance, corporate services)
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: Vice-presidents set spending levels, act as witnesses and attend settlement. Averaged over five years.

roles.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: Presents the business plan to the board and signs off the filing.
System planning engineers write the Distribution System Plan that supports the capital request (s5); averaged over five years.
Accountants and budget analysts build the OM&A, rate base and revenue requirement figures and answer finance interrogatories; averaged over five years.
In-house counsel reviews evidence, leads settlement drafting and argument; outside regulatory counsel is often retained as well (not modelled as a role).

systems.name: ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Asset condition and health index analytics
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Document management and engineering drawing repository
OEB RRR and regulatory e-filing portal

steps.name: Set up the rate application project
steps.description: The regulatory manager confirms that the current rate plan ends and that the utility will rebase on a five-year Custom IR, writes the workplan and timeline back from the target filing date, names a lead for each exhibit, and drafts the scope for outside benchmarking studies and the customer engagement vendor.

error.defect_description: Workplan underestimates the time needed for engagement or benchmarking.

evidence.note: Custom IR choice, outside benchmarking studies and engagement vendor described in s5; effort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Executive approves strategy, budget and consultants
steps.description: The vice-president responsible for regulatory affairs reviews the proposed plan type, the budget for consultants and the engagement approach with the executive team, and approves the procurement of the benchmarking studies and the customer engagement vendor.

control.basis: Delegation of authority for consulting spend and corporate rate strategy

evidence.note: Typical executive approval; timing estimated.

steps.name: Vendor runs first phase of customer engagement
steps.description: The engagement vendor, procured and briefed by the regulatory team, runs focus groups and surveys on customers' priorities across rate classes. The regulatory team waits for results, reviews the draft report and passes the findings to the planners.

evidence.note: Engagement launched January 2019 and ran through September 2019 in two phases (s5); the wait runs from project set-up in late summer 2018 through vendor procurement, mobilisation and phase I fieldwork to spring 2019, which is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Planning engineers build the Distribution System Plan
steps.description: System planning engineers turn asset condition, load forecasts and the capital plan into the five-year Distribution System Plan: investment categories, project lists, pacing options and the business cases that justify each program, using the asset analytics and GIS data.

error.defect_description: Capital forecast does not reconcile with the plan used for the revenue requirement.

evidence.note: DSP supports average capital of $100.8M a year (s5); effort of about 350 hours each for six engineers is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Finance builds OM&A, rate base and revenue requirement
steps.description: Accountants and budget analysts build the test-year OM&A by program, the five-year rate base and depreciation, cost of capital and taxes, and run the revenue requirement, load forecast and cost allocation models side by side with the planners' capital forecast.

error.defect_description: Model links break or OM&A and capital figures differ between exhibits.

evidence.note: OM&A and revenue requirement figures in s2 and s5; effort estimated.

steps.name: Vendor runs second phase of engagement on spending options
steps.description: The vendor surveys customers in every class on the reference plan and on faster or slower spending scenarios with their bill impacts, then reports support by class. The regulatory team reviews the questionnaire and the results.

evidence.note: Second phase surveyed customers on options and trade-offs; nearly 21,000 took part (s5).

steps.name: Executive team settles the business plan
steps.description: The vice-presidents compare the engagement results, benchmarking studies and bill impacts, decide the spending level for each program, and sign off the business plan and the numbers the application will carry.

error.defect_description: A late change to spending levels forces model reruns.

evidence.note: Business plan informed by benchmarking and engagement (s5); time estimated.

steps.name: Board of directors approves the business plan
steps.description: The CEO presents the business plan and rate strategy to the board of directors at a scheduled meeting. The board approves it or asks for changes to spending or rate impacts before the filing goes ahead.

control.basis: Board of directors approval of the business plan under the corporate governance framework

evidence.note: Business plan approved by the board on November 28, 2019 (s5); rework share estimated.

steps.name: Regulatory analysts draft exhibits and OEB workforms
steps.description: Analysts write the exhibits in the order of the filing requirements (administration, rate base, OM&A, cost of capital, load forecast, cost allocation, rate design, deferral accounts) and complete the OEB Chapter 2 appendices, revenue requirement workform, cost allocation model and bill impact model.

error.defect_description: Inconsistent figures, missing filing requirement items or stale references between exhibits.

control.basis: OEB Filing Requirements for Electricity Distribution Rate Applications, Chapters 2, 3 and 5

evidence.note: Filing requirements and workbooks named in s4 and s5; effort of about 450 hours each for seven analysts is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review exhibits for completeness and consistency
steps.description: The regulatory manager and legal counsel read every exhibit against the filing requirements checklist, trace each key number back to the models, and mark gaps, contradictions and wording that could create hearing risk. Exhibits with problems go back to their authors.

evidence.note: Typical review cycle; effort and rework share estimated.

steps.name: Fix gaps and cross-references
steps.description: Analysts and the exhibit authors correct the numbers, add missing filing-requirement items and update cross-references and the models, then return the exhibits for another review.

error.defect_description: A fix in one exhibit is not carried to the others.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Executive signs off and files the application
steps.description: The vice-president and CEO confirm the application, the regulatory team assembles the evidence, workbooks and attachments and files it electronically with the OEB, serving it on past intervenors.

control.basis: Ontario Energy Board Act, 1998, section 78: distribution rates require an OEB order

evidence.note: Application filed February 11, 2020 under section 78 (s1).

steps.name: OEB checks completeness, issues notice and admits intervenors
steps.description: OEB staff check the application for completeness, the OEB issues a Notice of Hearing that the utility publishes and serves, parties apply to intervene, and the OEB issues Procedural Order No. 1 setting the interrogatory schedule.

control.basis: OEB Rules of Practice and Procedure: notice, intervention and procedural orders

evidence.note: Filed February 11, notice March 4, Procedural Order No. 1 March 31, 2020 (s1): 49 days. The OEB standard allows 14 days to completeness and 35 more to Procedural Order No. 1 (s6).

steps.name: Update the application for prior-year actuals
steps.description: Once the prior year's financial statements are audited, analysts replace bridge-year forecasts with actuals in the rate base, OM&A and deferral account schedules, rerun the workforms and file an updated application.

error.defect_description: Updated figures not carried into every schedule.

evidence.note: Updated application with 2019 actuals filed May 5, 2020 (s1); effort estimated.

steps.name: Receive interrogatories from OEB staff and intervenors
steps.description: OEB staff and the intervenors send written interrogatories on every exhibit, and OEB staff file their own benchmarking expert evidence that the utility must also answer. The regulatory team logs and assigns each question.

evidence.note: Eight intervenors and PEG expert evidence filed June 19, 2020 (s1); interrogatory preparation hours disputed in cost claims (s3).

steps.name: Regulatory analysts coordinate and draft interrogatory responses
steps.description: Analysts split the interrogatories by exhibit, draft responses on rates, deferral accounts and rate design, chase subject experts for the rest, and keep a tracker so every response is consistent with the evidence and with other responses.

error.defect_description: Responses contradict each other or the evidence.

evidence.note: Typical; the OEB standard allows about 20 days for responses (s6 gives day 60 to day 80).

steps.name: Planning engineers answer capital and DSP interrogatories
steps.description: Planning engineers answer the questions on project need, pacing, asset condition and unit costs, pulling data from the asset analytics tool and GIS, at the same time as the regulatory analysts work on the rest.

error.defect_description: Asset data in responses differs from the DSP.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Accountants answer finance and OM&A interrogatories
steps.description: Accountants answer the questions on OM&A variances, compensation, rate base, depreciation and taxes, at the same time as the other response teams, and reconcile every number to the updated application.

error.defect_description: A variance explanation does not tie to the ledger.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Review and file interrogatory responses
steps.description: Legal counsel and the regulatory manager review every response for accuracy, consistency and confidential information, send weak responses back, and file the full set on the OEB record by the deadline.

control.basis: OEB procedural order deadlines for interrogatory responses

evidence.note: Typical; time estimated.

steps.name: Witness panels answer questions at the technical conference
steps.description: Vice-presidents and senior staff sit as witness panels over several days while OEB staff and intervenor counsel ask follow-up questions, and note undertakings to provide more information.

evidence.note: Technical conference held July 15-17 and July 21, 2020 (s1); people per panel estimated.

steps.name: Answer technical conference undertakings
steps.description: Analysts and subject experts write answers to each undertaking from the technical conference, rerun models where asked, and file them before the settlement conference.

error.defect_description: A rerun changes numbers already in responses.

evidence.note: Estimated.

steps.name: Negotiate at the settlement conference
steps.description: Executives, counsel and the regulatory manager negotiate with intervenors over several days, trading reductions in OM&A and capital, ratepayer protection mechanisms and rate design, and test each offer against the revenue requirement model.

next.condition: settlement on all or most issues

evidence.note: Settlement conference August 10-14 and 17, 2020, reaching agreement on all but one issue (s1, s2); share without settlement estimated.

steps.name: Draft and file the settlement proposal
steps.description: Legal counsel drafts the settlement proposal issue by issue with the intervenors' counsel, analysts update the models and bill impacts to match, and the signed proposal is filed with the OEB.

error.defect_description: Model figures in the proposal do not match the agreed terms.

evidence.note: Settlement proposal dated September 18, 2020, about a month after the conference (s1).

steps.name: OEB reviews the settlement proposal
steps.description: OEB staff file a submission on the proposal and the panel decides whether to accept it, and sets a written or oral process for any unsettled issue.

next.condition: accepted with an unsettled issue for written hearing

evidence.note: Proposal accepted October 2, 2020 with one issue sent to a written hearing (s1, s2); the shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare witnesses and attend the oral hearing
steps.description: Counsel prepares witness panels, writes the opening, and the panels are cross-examined over several hearing days on the unsettled issues.

evidence.note: Oral hearing slot at day 130 of the OEB standard schedule (s6); effort estimated.

steps.name: Write argument on the unsettled issues
steps.description: Counsel and the regulatory manager write the argument-in-chief on each unsettled issue, read the OEB staff and intervenor submissions that follow, and file a reply argument by the procedural deadline.

evidence.note: Written submissions on the unsettled issue were scheduled after October 2 (s1); argument steps run from day 140 to day 170 of the standard (s6).

steps.name: OEB issues its Decision and Order
steps.description: The OEB panel writes its reasons for accepting the settlement and its findings on unsettled issues and orders the utility to file a draft rate order with bill impacts.

evidence.note: Decision and Order issued November 19, 2020, 48 days after the settlement decision (s1).

steps.name: Prepare the draft rate order and tariff sheets
steps.description: Analysts rerun the revenue requirement, cost allocation, rate design, retail transmission and deferral account workbooks to the decision, produce the five-year tariff sheets and bill impacts by class, and file the draft rate order.

error.defect_description: Tariff sheet or bill impact error found in comments.

evidence.note: Draft rate order filed December 3, 2020, 14 days after the decision, with the listed workbooks (s4); effort estimated.

steps.name: Parties comment and the OEB issues the final rate order
steps.description: OEB staff and intervenors comment on the draft rate order, the utility replies and corrects any errors, and the OEB issues the final rate order and approved tariff for the January 1 effective date.

evidence.note: The standard allows 25 days from draft to final rate order (s6). The time to Hydro Ottawa's final order is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hand the rate order to rate implementation and the board
steps.description: The regulatory manager circulates the final rate order and tariff to billing, customer service and communications for loading and customer notices, briefs the executive and board on the outcome, and opens the cost claims and annual update calendar.

evidence.note: Rate order leads to annual implementation applications (s1); cost awards to intervenors decided February 18, 2021 (s3).

exceptions.name: Board sends the business plan back
exceptions.description: The board asks for lower spending or rate impacts, so the executive team reworks the plan before filing.

exceptions.name: Exhibits fail internal review
exceptions.description: Exhibits go back to authors for missing filing requirement items or inconsistent numbers, sometimes more than once.

exceptions.name: No settlement on major issues
exceptions.description: Settlement fails or the OEB rejects the proposal, so the case goes to an oral hearing with witness preparation and cross-examination.

exceptions.name: Draft rate order needs corrections
exceptions.description: Comments on the draft rate order find tariff or bill impact errors that must be fixed before the final order.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from project set-up to final rate order

evidence.note: Anchored on published milestones: engagement launched January 2019 (s5), filing February 11, 2020, decision November 19, 2020 (s1), draft rate order December 3, 2020 (s4). Project set-up about three to five months before engagement and final order about a month after the draft are the author's estimates.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from filing to Decision and Order

evidence.note: February 11 to November 19, 2020.

benchmarks.population: OEB performance standard for cost-based applications under $500M revenue requirement

evidence.note: Decision at day 230 and final rate order at day 275 after the completeness letter.

benchmarks.unit: customers taking part in rate engagement

evidence.note: Nearly 21,000.

pain_points.description: The same figures (capital, OM&A, rate base, load) live in many linked spreadsheets and exhibits, so a late change to the business plan or the prior-year actuals ripples through every schedule and causes review rework.

evidence.note: The draft rate order alone carried ten live workbooks (s4); rework shares estimated.

pain_points.description: Most of the elapsed time is waiting: customer engagement fieldwork, board meeting dates and the OEB's procedural calendar set the pace, not the utility's work.

evidence.note: Dates in s1 and s5.

pain_points.description: Interrogatories from eight intervenors and OEB staff arrive at once and must be answered in about three weeks, pulling engineers and accountants off their normal work.

evidence.note: Eight intervenors (s1, s3); 20-day response window in the standard schedule (s6).

sources.title: Decision and Order, EB-2019-0261, Hydro Ottawa Limited (2021-2025 rates)
sources.supports: Process dates: application filed February 11, 2020; Notice of Hearing March 4; Procedural Order No. 1 March 31 (interrogatories, expert evidence); updated application with 2019 actuals May 5; OEB staff expert (PEG) evidence June 19; issues list June 22; technical conference July 15-17 and 21; settlement conference August 10-14 and 17; settlement proposal accepted October 2; Decision and Order November 19, 2020; eight intervenors; 15 letters of comment; Custom IR framework components; draft rate order with bill impacts required.

sources.title: Backgrounder: Decision and Order EB-2019-0261, Hydro Ottawa Limited
sources.supports: Settlement reached on all but one issue (fixed/variable rate design for three large commercial classes), which went to a written hearing; $5.4M reduction to the proposed 2021 base revenue requirement of $203.9M; $3.3M OM&A reduction; capital additions of $555.1M over the term; nearly all major rate hearings include settlement conferences, many reaching full settlement.

sources.title: Decision and Order on Cost Awards, EB-2019-0261
sources.supports: Eight intervenors with cost eligibility (BOMA, CCC, DRC, Energy Probe, Environmental Defence, Pollution Probe, SEC, VECC); cost awards of about $24,000 to $66,000 per intervenor paid by the utility; dispute over hours claimed for interrogatory preparation; COVID-19 moved the proceeding to virtual and electronic-only filing.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa Limited Custom IR application, Draft Rate Order (EB-2019-0261), filed December 3, 2020
sources.supports: Draft rate order filed two weeks after the decision, with live Excel workbooks: Chapter 2 appendices, tariff schedule and bill impacts model, revenue requirement workforms, deferral and variance account continuity schedule, RTSR workform, cost allocation model, PILs workforms, low voltage rate design; signed by the Director, Regulatory Affairs.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, Updated Executive Summary (Exhibit 1-1-8, EB-2019-0261)
sources.supports: Application prepared under OEB Chapter 2, 3 and 5 filing requirements; business plan approved by the board of directors on November 28, 2019; rate-specific customer engagement launched January 2019 and ran to September 2019 in two phases, with nearly 21,000 participants; third-party benchmarking studies (econometric total cost, unit cost, IT budget, market compensation) commissioned for the business plan; Distribution System Plan supports capital of about $100.8M a year.

sources.title: Performance Standards for Processing Applications: Rates, Cost Based <$500 Million Annual Revenue Requirement
sources.supports: Standard schedule in calendar days from the completeness letter: interrogatories day 60, responses day 80, settlement conference day 90, settlement proposal day 115, decision day 230, draft rate order day 250, final rate order day 275; application filed 14 days before the completeness letter.

assumptions: Labour figures cover internal staff only. Outside consultants (engagement vendor, benchmarking firms, outside counsel) appear as waits or are folded into internal steps; their fees are not in the labour cost.
fte_on_process is averaged over the five-year cycle, because the process runs once every five years; in the two busy years the regulatory team spends most of its time on the application.

touch_min on team steps is the working time of each person; the simulator counts it as elapsed time, so drafting steps that in practice spread over months have shorter waits to compensate. The cycle-time benchmark is a tier C estimate built from tier A milestones.

The application is modelled on one real case (Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025), so branch shares for settlement and hearing outcomes are estimates for Ontario practice, drawn from the OEB's statement that nearly all major rate hearings include settlement conferences and many settle fully (s2).
The final Decision and Rate Order date (about five weeks after the draft rate order) is an estimate; the document itself was not opened.
Annual rate updates in years two to five are a separate process (fin-annual-rate-update) and are not part of this workflow.
